chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
**Problem:** What is the molarity of the solution when there is $20\text{ g } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $250\text{ mL}$ solution?

**Solution:** Molecular mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = 23 \times 2 + 12 + 16 \times 3 = 106$

$1$ molarity in $1$ liter solution requires $106$ gram

$1$ molarity in $250\text{ mL}$ solution requires $\frac{106 \times 250}{1000} = 26.5$ gram

$26.5\text{ g } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $250\text{ mL}$ makes the molarity $1$ molar

$1\text{ g } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $250\text{ mL}$ makes the molarity $\frac{1}{26.5}$ molar

$20\text{ g } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $250\text{ mL}$ makes the molarity $\frac{1 \times 20}{26.5} = 0.75$ molar

**Alternative Way**
$$\begin{aligned}
w &= \frac{SVM}{1000} \\
20 &= \frac{S \times 250 \times 106}{1000} \\
S &= 0.75\text{ molar}
\end{aligned}$$

**Problem:** What is the volume of the solution in mililiter when $20\text{ g } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is dissolved in $0.75\text{ molar } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution?

**Solution:** Given here, $S = 0.75$ molar, $w = 20\text{ g}$, $M = 23 \times 2 + 12 + 16 \times 3 = 106$, $V = ?$

We know, $w = \frac{SVM}{1000}$

$$20 = \frac{0.75 \times V \times 106}{1000}$$
